newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom spikes up after Q3 result.
newsitem.headline: Telecom spikes up after Q3 result.

text.p: Shares in Telecom Corp of New Zealand Ltd shot up 10 cents to NZ$6.96 on Tuesday after the company issued its third quarter result, with initial analysis suggested the utility's core earnings were intact.
Telecom earlier reported a slight rise in nine-month earnings to NZ$528.1 million from $520.2 million, raising the dividend to 9.5 cents a share from 8.5.
Telecom had been under downward pressure for several weeks in the lead-up to the result and the bearish tone was made worse by last week's credit rating downgrade by Standard and Poor's.
Nigel Scott, head dealer with brokers BZW, said his initial reaction was that the result appeared to show core earnings were intact.
"With the dividend being increased and some pretty strong rhetoric about cost cutting, the market may have just gained a little bit of confidence," he said.
But with key U.S. investors absent due to the President's Day holiday on Monday, the market's final analysis was difficult to gauge, he said.
Campbell Stuart, head of equities at SBC Warburg, said the result was within the range of expectations, although slightly lower than SBC had expected.
"But there are a lot of one-offs in there. There is still genuine growth, there is still growth in cellular," he said.
"Call growth and enhanced services are still going quite well. Costs are a bit higher, but if you back out some one-offs it is still a pretty robust result," Stuart said.
While there was further assessment needed, the stock had potentially been oversold over the last few weeks, he said.
